_comment: Issue #218: the whole book on the timeline for a multi-file audiobook. Subject is the header-only src/core/BookTimeline.h -- the total derived from part sizes and one measured duration, the absorption that keeps that total from jittering at fifty-six part boundaries, the monotonicity of the elapsed reading across one, and the clamp that keeps a drag inside the part the app is actually holding. probe_booktimeline asserts them.

mutants.name: the-total-jitters-at-every-boundary
mutants._why: THE decision this feature turns on, restated as a mutation: stop absorbing a measurement's error into the parts not yet heard and the total moves at each of fifty-six boundaries. The issue says in as many words that a number which visibly changes at every part is worse than the bug it replaced.

mutants.name: the-measurement-does-not-win
mutants._why: The part keeps its ESTIMATE while mpv is telling us its real length. The published boundary then disagrees with the file by however much the estimate was out, so the elapsed reading jumps -- backwards if the estimate was short -- at every chapter.
mutants.find:
const double delta = seconds - lengths_.at(k);
        lengths_[k] = seconds;

mutants.name: the-correction-is-taken-out-of-parts-already-heard
mutants._why: Absorbing across the WHOLE book instead of the tail. It looks more even-handed and it is the defect: it moves the offsets of parts behind the play head, so the position the listener is at changes underneath them and the boundary they just crossed goes backwards.
mutants.find:
for (int i = k + 1; i < lengths_.size(); ++i)
            if (!measured_.at(i)) lengths_[i] *= scale;
mutants.replace:
for (int i = 0; i < lengths_.size(); ++i)
            if (!measured_.at(i)) lengths_[i] *= scale;

mutants.name: the-unheard-tail-may-be-squeezed-to-nothing
mutants._why: Without the guard a correction larger than everything left to hear scales the remaining parts to zero or negative: the bar pegs at the end of the book while a part is still playing, and every later position reads as 'finished'.

mutants.name: a-drag-may-leave-the-part-in-hand
mutants._why: The clamp gone: a book-scale gesture is passed through as a position in a file the player is not holding. mpv seeks to the end of the current part instead, so the bar is a control that does something other than what it showed. Crossing a part means minting its link, which #216 measured at sixty-five seconds and no link.

mutants.name: a-position-past-the-part-runs-into-the-next-one
mutants._why: mpv reports a hair over the duration it declared often enough to matter. Unclamped, the last tick of part three reads as the first second of part four -- the reading crosses a boundary the playback has not.
mutants.find: const double p = positionInPart < 0.0 ? 0.0 : (positionInPart > len ? len : positionInPart);

mutants.name: a-release-missing-one-size-still-gets-a-total
mutants._why: The issue's own fallback rule deleted. A part with no size is priced at zero seconds, so the book is shown as shorter than it is and every position past that part is wrong -- a total nothing supports, which is worse than the per-part display it replaced.

mutants.name: a-bare-number-in-the-subtitle-is-read-as-a-size
mutants._why: The field is a general subtitle. Without the unit requirement a row reading 'S1 E2' or a bitrate would answer a byte count, and a whole book's timeline would be built out of a number that is not a size at all.
mutants.find:
if (unit == QLatin1String("T") || unit == QLatin1String("TB") || unit == QLatin1String("TIB")) return value * 1024.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0;
    return 0.0;
mutants.replace:
if (unit == QLatin1String("T") || unit == QLatin1String("TB") || unit == QLatin1String("TIB")) return value * 1024.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0 * 1024.0;
    return value;

mutants.name: a-decimal-comma-is-read-as-a-group-separator
mutants._why: The size string is formatted by a server under whatever culture it runs in. Taking only '.' as the decimal point turns '42,19 MB' into 4219 MB -- a hundredfold error in one part's share of the book, silently, on exactly the installs that would never see it tested.
mutants.find: const int dec = lastDot > lastCom ? lastDot : lastCom;

mutants.name: a-single-file-release-gets-a-book-scale-bar
mutants._why: One file already shows the whole of itself -- that is the case this issue exists to give the others. Treating it as a book routes a .m4b through a derived timeline instead of mpv's exact one, which is the constraint the issue states first: the single-file case must not change at all.

mutants.name: a-part-offset-includes-the-part-itself
mutants._why: An off-by-one in the one sum everything else is measured from: the reading would start each part a whole part further on, so the bar jumps forward at every boundary and reaches the end of the book with a part still to play.
mutants.find: for (int k = 0; k < i && k < lengths_.size(); ++k) at += lengths_.at(k);
mutants.replace: for (int k = 0; k <= i && k < lengths_.size(); ++k) at += lengths_.at(k);
